On this page

Command Line Interface ​

Saidi ships two executables and a set of npm scripts. The executables are thin launchers: neither parses command-line flags, so everything you configure comes from the environment, config/settings.json, or the Settings UI. This page lists what the code actually reads.

Binaries ​

package.json declares two entries:

json
"bin": {
  "saidi": "./bin/saidi.js",
  "saidi-marketplace": "./bin/saidi-marketplace.js"
}

saidi ​

bash
saidi

bin/saidi.js is a supervisor. It runs the orchestrator server as a child process, watches it, and relaunches it when the server asks for a fresh boot. It takes no arguments and no flags — process.argv is never read.

What it does on startup:

  1. process.chdir() to the package root, because the server reads .env and client/dist relative to process.cwd() and a global install can be launched from anywhere.
  2. Resolve the data dir, mirroring src/orchestrator/config.ts: SAIDI_HOME → (if SAIDI_DEV) the package root → ~/.saidi.
  3. Resolve the port for the browser URL: PORT → config/settings.json port → 4317. The host follows the same shape: HOST → settings.json host → 127.0.0.1.
  4. Choose the runtime — dist/server.js with plain Node when the bundle exists and SAIDI_DEV is unset, otherwise node --import tsx src/orchestrator/server.ts.
  5. Spawn the child, and on the first launch only, wait up to 20 s for the port to accept a TCP connection, then open http://localhost:<port>/ in the default browser (open on macOS, start on Windows, xdg-open elsewhere). Skipped entirely when SAIDI_DEV is set, because dev serves the UI from Vite on 5317.

Environment it reads:

VariableEffect
SAIDI_HOMEData dir override, resolved to an absolute path
SAIDI_DEVRun from source via tsx, keep state in the package root, skip the browser open
PORTPort used for the browser URL and the listen probe
HOSTHost used for the listen probe (0.0.0.0 probes 127.0.0.1)

Environment it sets on the child:

VariableValue
SAIDI_SUPERVISED1 — tells the server its self-restart path is safe to take
SAIDI_RUNTIMEdist or src — tells the server whether npm i -g would replace the running code

Signals: SIGINT and SIGTERM are forwarded to the child; the supervisor exits once the child does.

saidi-marketplace ​

bash
saidi-marketplace

bin/saidi-marketplace.js runs the standalone hosted-marketplace service. Same shape as saidi but without the supervision: it anchors cwd to the package root, picks dist/marketplace-server.js when it exists and SAIDI_DEV is unset, otherwise node --import tsx src/marketplace/server/index.ts, forwards SIGINT and SIGTERM, and propagates the child's exit code. No flags are parsed; only SAIDI_DEV is read.

The supervisor ​

bin/supervisor.js is not an executable — it is the pure decision module that bin/saidi.js imports. Factoring it out keeps the relaunch rules unit-testable without spawning anything (bin/supervisor.test.ts).

decideRestart(code, restartTimestamps, now, ctx) returns one of four actions:

Child exit codeActionBehaviour
75 (RESTART_EXIT_CODE)relaunchThe server asked for a fresh boot (new MONGODB_URI, re-hydrated env, an agent or memory import). The old child fully exits first, so the port is released before the new one binds
76 (UPDATE_EXIT_CODE)updateInstall the update, then relaunch
anything elseexitClean stop or crash — propagated, never relaunched
any, post-updaterollbackA freshly updated child that died before proving itself
ConstantValueMeaning
MAX_RESTARTS3Relaunches allowed inside the window
WINDOW_MS10_000The crash-loop window
HEALTHY_MS60_000How long an updated child must survive before the rollback net is disarmed

The update install deliberately happens in the supervisor, between spawns: npm i -g deletes and rewrites the very package directory the server executes from, so doing it in-process would swap the code under a live server. The package installed is github:saeed9321/saidi-agent; a rollback reinstalls github:saeed9321/saidi-agent#v<version>. An install failure (offline, EACCES on a root-owned prefix) is non-fatal and leaves the current version in place.

The rollback check runs before the crash-loop guard and bypasses it — a broken release that dies instantly would otherwise trip the guard and leave the app down, which is the outage rollback exists to prevent. It is one-shot: if the old version also fails, the exit code propagates normally.

Running ​

ScriptCommandNotes

dev:clientnpm --prefix client run devVite dev server on port 5317

start:marketplace:prodnode dist/marketplace-server.jsMarketplace service from the bundle

ScriptCommandOutput
buildbuild:client then build:serverThe normal full build
build:clientnpm --prefix client run buildclient/dist/

Maintenance ​

ScriptCommandNotes
setupnpm install && npm --prefix client installInstall both dependency trees
preparenpm --prefix client install && npm run buildnpm lifecycle hook — installs the client and builds on install
typechecktsc --noEmit && npm --prefix client run typecheckServer and client, no emit

Node 20 or newer is required (engines.node: ">=20"). See Installation for a first run.

Build scripts ​

All three bundlers use esbuild with the same settings: bundle: true, platform: "node", format: "esm", target: "node20", minify: true, and packages: "external". Keeping npm packages external means only Saidi's own first-party source is bundled (and thus hidden), while native modules and the agent CLI the Claude Agent SDK spawns are installed from the registry at the destination and keep working exactly as they do from source.

Each carries a small resolve plugin that maps relative ./foo.js / ../bar.js imports to the sibling foo.ts when it exists, because the source uses NodeNext-style .js specifiers that actually point at .ts files.

ScriptEntry pointOutput
scripts/build-server.mjssrc/orchestrator/server.tsdist/server.js
scripts/build-marketplace.mjssrc/marketplace/server/index.tsdist/marketplace-server.js
scripts/build-sandbox-worker.mjssrc/orchestrator/sandbox/worker.tsdist/sandbox-worker.js

The sandbox worker keeps packages external for a second reason: the sandbox image installs @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk from npm so it gets the Linux platform binary the SDK spawns — bundling the host's build would not run in the container.

scripts/build-dist.mjs ​

Assembles the source-free publishable artifact into staging-dist/. It fails fast if dist/server.js or client/dist/index.html is missing, so run the builds first. The staging tree contains dist/, client/dist/, bin/{saidi.js,supervisor.js}, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, and a minimal package.json carrying runtime dependencies only — no src/, .env, agents/, memory/, or config/. As a guard it walks the finished tree and throws if any .ts or .tsx file leaked in. See Deployment for what to do with the result.

scripts/obsidian-vault.mjs ​

bash
npm run vault

Generates a read-only Obsidian mirror of the memory dir: memory/INDEX.md (a hub note wikilinking every project and agent memory note, with fact counts and last-modified dates) and memory/.obsidian/app.json (ignore filters for runs/, chat/, chat-uploads/, members/ and .obsidian/, merged rather than overwritten so settings changed inside Obsidian survive). Nothing is read back — edits made in Obsidian are never synced. It refuses to run when SAIDI_CLOUD=1, because in cloud each org has its own memory dir and there is no single vault. It reads SAIDI_HOME from the environment or, failing that, parses .env itself.

Maintenance scripts ​

These are not wired into npm scripts; run them directly. Each resolves the Mongo server the same way the app does (MONGODB_URI → memory/secrets.json → localhost) and the database name from SAIDI_CLOUD. Back up MongoDB before any of them writes.

scripts/cleanup-unscoped.mjs ​

Removes DB records that are not scoped to an organization, so a cloud database is cleanly multi-tenant.

bash
node --import tsx scripts/cleanup-unscoped.mjs        # dry run — counts only
node --import tsx scripts/cleanup-unscoped.mjs --yes  # actually delete
FlagEffect
--yesApply the deletions. Without it the script is a dry run

It deletes orgless AgentDef documents, orgless records in the org-scoped collections (runs, chats, crons, reflexes, activity, memory, credit ledger), and the single local-mode credit wallet keyed default. It keeps the four owner-managed platform documents (settings, secrets, provider-profiles, scan-roots), every record that has an orgId, and all auth records. Idempotent.

scripts/consolidate-creative-roster.mjs ​

A one-shot roster consolidation that updates both the Mongo agent documents and the materialized disk copy — a disk-only cleanup would revert on the next boot, because agent dirs are rebuilt from Mongo.

bash
node --import tsx scripts/consolidate-creative-roster.mjs        # dry run
node --import tsx scripts/consolidate-creative-roster.mjs --yes  # apply
SAIDI_ORG_ID=<org> node --import tsx scripts/consolidate-creative-roster.mjs --yes
Flag / variableEffect
--yesApply; otherwise dry run
SAIDI_ORG_IDTarget org; defaults to local

Restart the server afterwards so it re-materializes the corrected roster.

scripts/migrate-to-cloud.mjs ​

Turns an existing single-user data set into organization #1 of a SAIDI_CLOUD=1 deployment.

bash
node scripts/migrate-to-cloud.mjs \
  --email you@example.com --org-name "Acme" --name "Said" --seats 5 [--dry-run]
FlagRequiredDefaultMeaning
--emailyes—Superadmin email (lowercased)
--org-nameyes—The organization's name
--namenoSaidSuperadmin display name
--seatsno5Seat count, floored at 1
--dry-runnooffReport without writing

The password comes from SAIDI_MIGRATE_PASSWORD (10+ characters), so it never lands in shell history. The script creates the user, org and owner membership, backfills orgId/createdBy onto runs, crons, reflexes, activity and the ledger, re-keys the credit wallet from default to the org id, and movesDATA_DIR/{memory,agents} under DATA_DIR/orgs/<orgId>/. It is idempotent — already-completed steps are detected and skipped.

scripts/run-baseline.mjs ​

Measures execution variance across repeated runs of the same brief: divergence is the headline metric, with cost and wall clock reported as p50/p95 because the interesting movement is in the tail.

bash
node scripts/run-baseline.mjs drive   --briefs briefs.json --reps 3 --out baseline.jsonl
node scripts/run-baseline.mjs analyze --out current.jsonl
node scripts/run-baseline.mjs compare before.jsonl after.jsonl
ModeBehaviour
driveStart each brief --reps times against a running Saidi, poll until settled, then measure
analyzeCompute the same metrics over runs already in the store; spends nothing
comparePrint a before/after table from two JSONL files

analyze is the default when no mode is given.

FlagDefaultMeaning
--briefs <file.json>—Required in drive mode. A JSON array of strings, or of { brief, project? } objects
--reps <n>3Repetitions per brief
--out <file>baseline.jsonlWhere rows are written
--base <url>SAIDI_BASE_URL or http://127.0.0.1:4317Server to drive
--cookie <cookie>SAIDI_COOKIE or emptySession cookie; needed in cloud mode, not locally
--timeout <ms>1200000 (20 min)How long to wait for a run to settle
--poll <ms>5000Poll interval while waiting

It talks to the same endpoints you would (HTTP API): POST /api/runs, GET /api/runs, GET /api/runs/:id. A run counts as settled once it reaches done, error, cancelled, awaiting_input or paused.

scripts/sync-version.mjs ​

Mirrors the root package.json version into client/package.json so the client bundle and the server report the same APP_VERSION. Run automatically by the npm version lifecycle hook during npm version <bump>; it takes no arguments.
